notYet: Not yet part of the Eastern Mediterranean

stages.name: Persian-held
stages.desc: Ruled by the Great King, through satraps and vassal kings

stages.name: Greek / Delian League
stages.desc: Free Greek city-states; from 477, Athens and its allies

stages.name: In revolt
stages.desc: Subjects of Persia in open rebellion

stages.name: Contested
stages.desc: Split between Persia and the Greeks, or fought over

stages.name: Battle site
stages.desc: A major battle by land or sea that year

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Ten kingdoms, Greek and Phoenician, under Persia; Phoenician Kition rules the south coast
Onesilus seizes Salamis; every city but Amathus joins the revolt
The Ionians beat the Phoenicians at sea off Salamis, but Onesilus falls on land
Soli falls after a five-month siege; Cyprus is Persian again
A Greek fleet under Pausanias subdues most of the island
Persia has the island back; Phoenician squadrons gather there before the Eurymedon
Athens sends two hundred ships to Cyprus, then diverts them to Egypt
The Athenians sail on to the Nile; Persia keeps the island
Cimon besieges Kition and dies; his fleet wins off Salamis
The Athenians withdraw; Cyprus stays Persian

states.name: Israel
timeline: Coastal towns under Persia, many tied to Tyre and Sidon
'Syrians of Palestine' sail in the Phoenician contingent, Herodotus says

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Sidon, Tyre and Byblos: Phoenician kings who serve the Great King with their fleets
Phoenician squadrons lead the fleet against Ionia
Tetramnestus of Sidon and Mattên of Tyre sail with Xerxes
Two hundred Phoenician ships lost at the Eurymedon
Athenians fight and die 'in Phoenicia', as their casualty list records
Phoenician yards build the fleet that will retake Egypt

states.name: Syria
timeline: Arwad, the island city off the Syrian coast, and the inland cities of the satrapy
Merbalus of Arwad commands the city's squadron in Xerxes' fleet

states.name: Turkey
timeline: The Ionian cities expel their tyrants and revolt against Persia
Lade: the Persian fleet, led by the Phoenicians, crushes the Ionians; Miletus is sacked
The Phoenician fleet takes the islands and the Hellespont; Ionia is reconquered
Xerxes' army crosses the Hellespont on bridges of Phoenician and Egyptian cables
Mycale: the Greeks burn the beached Persian fleet and Ionia rises again
The coastal Greek cities join Athens; the interior stays Persian
Eurymedon: Cimon destroys two hundred Phoenician triremes off Pamphylia
League cities on the coast, the satraps' Anatolia inland
The reported peace: no Persian warship west of Phaselis

states.name: Greece
timeline: Free Greek city-states; Athens and Eretria send ships to help the Ionian rebels
Mardonius brings Thrace and Macedon under Persia; the south stays free
Marathon: the Athenians defeat the Persian landing; Eretria is burned
The invaders withdraw; Persia still holds the north
Themistocles spends the Laurion silver on two hundred triremes
Thermopylae, Artemisium and Salamis; Athens is sacked, its fleet wins in the strait
Plataea: the Persian army in Greece is destroyed
The Persians are gone; the Greeks carry the war to sea
Athens leads the new Delian League, its treasury on Delos
The League's treasury moves from Delos to Athens

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Persian satrapy since 525; Egyptian squadrons serve beside the Phoenicians
Egypt revolts against Darius
Xerxes crushes the revolt
Inaros, a Libyan prince, raises Egypt and calls on Athens
An Athenian fleet sails up the Nile; the Persians hold out in Memphis
Megabyzus traps the Athenians at Prosopitis; Phoenicians destroy their relief squadron
Persia restores its rule; Amyrtaeus holds out in the marshes
Cimon sends sixty ships to help Amyrtaeus in the Delta
The Athenian ships go home

events.title: Ionian Revolt
events.text: Aristagoras of Miletus leads the Greek cities of Ionia in revolt against Persia.

events.title: Sardis burned
events.text: Ionians and Athenians burn the lower city of Sardis, seat of the satrap Artaphernes.

events.title: Cyprus rises
events.text: Onesilus seizes power in Salamis and brings the Cypriot cities into the revolt.

events.title: Siege of Amathus
events.text: Onesilus besieges Amathus, the one Cypriot city that stays loyal to Persia.

events.title: Battle off Cyprus
events.text: Ionian ships beat the Phoenician fleet off Salamis, but the Persians win on land and Onesilus is killed.

events.title: Fall of Soli
events.text: Soli holds out for five months before Persian miners bring down its walls.

events.title: The fleet musters
events.text: Sidon and Tyre fit out the squadrons that will lead six hundred ships against Ionia.

events.title: Battle of Lade
events.text: Off Miletus the Persian fleet, the Phoenicians most eager, crushes 353 Ionian triremes after the Samians desert.

events.title: Miletus sacked
events.text: Miletus falls; its men are killed and its women and children deported to the Persian Gulf.

events.title: Islands swept
events.text: The Phoenician fleet takes Chios, Lesbos and Tenedos and burns the Hellespont cities.

events.title: Miltiades escapes
events.text: Phoenician ships chase Miltiades out of the Chersonese and capture his son.

events.title: Wreck at Athos
events.text: A storm off Mount Athos wrecks Mardonius' fleet; Herodotus says three hundred ships were lost.

events.title: Eretria burned
events.text: A Persian fleet under Datis takes Eretria, burns its temples and enslaves its people.

events.title: Marathon
events.text: The Athenians and Plataeans defeat the Persian landing force on the plain of Marathon.

events.title: Egypt revolts
events.text: Egypt rises against Persia; Darius dies before he can march, and Xerxes retakes it in 484.

events.title: Athos canal
events.text: Xerxes has a canal dug across the Athos isthmus; Herodotus says the Phoenicians dug best.

events.title: Silver for ships
events.text: A rich silver strike at Laurion pays for Themistocles' two hundred new triremes.

events.title: Bridging the Hellespont
events.text: Phoenician flax and Egyptian papyrus cables hold the bridges that carry Xerxes' army into Europe.

events.title: Review at Doriscus
events.text: Xerxes reviews his fleet, 1,207 triremes in Herodotus, from a Sidonian ship under a golden canopy.

events.title: Storm off Sepias
events.text: A three-day gale wrecks at least four hundred Persian ships on the Magnesian coast.

events.title: Artemisium
events.text: The Greek and Persian fleets fight three days off northern Euboea; neither breaks.

events.title: Thermopylae
events.text: Leonidas and his rearguard die holding the pass as the Persian army breaks through.

events.title: Athens sacked
events.text: Xerxes takes the empty city and burns the temples on the Acropolis.

events.title: Battle of Salamis
events.text: In the strait, the Phoenicians on Xerxes' right meet the Athenians head-on and are routed.

events.title: Captains beheaded
events.text: Watching from the shore, Xerxes has Phoenician captains beheaded for blaming the Ionians, Herodotus says.

events.title: Plataea
events.text: The Greek allies destroy Mardonius' army in Boeotia; the invasion is over.

events.title: Mycale
events.text: The Greeks storm the Persian camp and burn its ships; the Phoenician squadrons had been sent home.

events.title: Pausanias in Cyprus
events.text: A Greek fleet under the Spartan Pausanias subdues most of Cyprus, then takes Byzantium.

events.title: Delian League
events.text: Athens and its allies swear an alliance against Persia, with a treasury on Delos.

events.title: Eion taken
events.text: Cimon captures Eion, Persia's fortress on the Strymon in Thrace.

events.title: The Persians
events.text: Aeschylus, a veteran of the battle, stages The Persians and gives Xerxes 1,207 ships.

events.title: Naxos crushed
events.text: Naxos tries to leave the League and is forced back in, the first ally made subject.

events.title: Eurymedon
events.text: Cimon destroys or captures two hundred Phoenician triremes and routs the army ashore.

events.title: Eighty more ships
events.text: Cimon then catches the eighty Phoenician ships coming from Cyprus and destroys them.

events.title: Inaros rebels
events.text: Inaros, a Libyan prince, raises western Egypt against Persia and calls on Athens.

events.title: Athens on the Nile
events.text: Two hundred Athenian and allied ships sail up the Nile and take most of Memphis.

events.title: Fallen in Phoenicia
events.text: An Athenian tribe lists its dead of one year in Cyprus, in Egypt and in Phoenicia.

events.title: Prosopitis
events.text: After an eighteen-month siege on a Nile island, the Athenian expedition is destroyed.

events.title: Mendesian ambush
events.text: Phoenician ships destroy most of fifty Athenian relief triremes at the Mendesian mouth of the Nile.

events.title: Treasury to Athens
events.text: The League's treasury moves from Delos to Athens, now the master of an empire.

events.title: Siege of Kition
events.text: Cimon besieges Phoenician Kition with two hundred ships and dies there, of sickness or a wound.

events.title: Salamis in Cyprus
events.text: Sailing home, the Athenians defeat the Phoenician, Cypriot and Cilician fleet at sea and on land.

events.title: Peace of Callias
events.text: Later writers say Callias made peace with Persia: no royal warship west of Phaselis. Thucydides never mentions it.

chartNote: Regions are today's countries, a convenient grid; no such borders existed in antiquity. Each is coloured by who held most of it in a given year, a simplification: Turkey covers both the Greek cities of the coast and the Persian interior, and Greece includes Thrace and Macedon, held by Persia from 492 to 479 BC. 'Battle site' marks the year of a major battle. Dates follow Herodotus, Thucydides and Diodorus and are often uncertain by a year or more.
